anomalies.description: A sudden, intense flash of white light with visible sparks and rapid expansion occurs at the location of the object on the metal surface, consistent with a small-scale explosion or violent ignition.

A sudden ignition and sustained combustion of a small object on a metal surface, producing a bright flame and molten material; the rapid onset and intensity suggest a small-scale energetic reaction (e.g., battery thermal runaway), consistent with an explosion event in the defined sense (sudden blast/energy release).

A sudden, intense flash of light and sparks erupts from a small device on a metal surface, rapidly overexposing the frame—consistent with an electrical or chemical explosion (e.g., battery rupture). The event begins at ~44.0 s with initial sparks and culminates in full whiteout by 45.0 s, persisting through 47.5 s.

A sudden, intense bright flash with flying sparks and rapid overexposure, consistent with a metal cutting or welding operation causing a localized explosive-like reaction (e.g., thermite or high-energy arc). The event begins at f0 with visible sparks and a tool on metal, then rapidly escalates to full whiteout by f2–f6, and remains intensely luminous with visible sparks through f15.
